name: Rail-mounted transfer arm (linear track)
status_line: Not in PyLabRobot yet, the maker's SDK documents it. The example writes the class.
reaches: Through the xArm controller with xarm-python-sdk: the same XArmAPI object as the arm calls get/set_linear_motor_*; the SDK sends them as Modbus to the control box RS-485 (xarm-python-sdk xarm/x3/linear_motor.py:40-46).
decoded_from: Nothing decoded. Names, units and return codes come from xarm-python-sdk 1.18.4 (xarm-python-sdk xarm/wrapper/xarm_api.py:3648-3805, xarm-python-sdk xarm/x3/linear_motor.py:82-219, xarm-python-sdk xarm/x3/code.py:52-54). A search of PyLabRobot 182f92e for linear track or linear motor finds nothing.
steps: Read the track calls in the SDK: get_linear_motor_pos/status/error/on_zero/is_enabled and set_linear_motor_enable/back_origin/pos (xarm-python-sdk xarm/wrapper/xarm_api.py:3648-3805).
Write 1 plain class with async setup() and stop(); stop() restores the enable state setup() found (docs/contributor_guide/device-driver-guide.md:22-23).
Expose intent only: home() and move_to(mm) read the state, act only if needed, then confirm (docs/contributor_guide/device-driver-guide.md:39-41).
Issue moves with wait=False and confirm in Python: error register, then motion bit 0 clear (xarm-python-sdk xarm/wrapper/xarm_api.py:3669-3670), then the position report.
Log a warning in setup() that it is unverified (docs/contributor_guide/device-driver-guide.md:45-47); test it against a simulated SDK object first.
Teach the station positions on the real track and set a measured reply timeout before any real run.
scenario: Home the track if it is not homed, travel to a taught station at 450 mm and 200 mm/s, confirm the arrival from the position report. Positions and speed are made up.
real: Method names, arguments, units and return codes copied from xarm-python-sdk 1.18.4
Error register titles copied from the SDK code table
simulated: The SDK object: position, enable, homed, motion and error registers
Instant motion. lost_reply: the move runs, the position report after it never returns
not_checked: Real travel times and a sane timeout
limits: The SDK refuses set_linear_motor_pos with code 82 until on_zero is 1, so on_zero acts as a homed flag (xarm-python-sdk xarm/x3/linear_motor.py:158-161).
The SDK sends int(pos*2000) (xarm-python-sdk xarm/x3/linear_motor.py:166) but reports position as round(raw/2000), whole mm (xarm-python-sdk xarm/x3/linear_motor.py:58).
Stroke depends on the serial number: 0..700, 0..1000 or 0..1500 mm; speed 1..1000 mm/s (xarm-python-sdk xarm/wrapper/xarm_api.py:3795-3799).
The SDK's own wait polls every 0.1 s for up to 100 s by default and returns 80 on any error register (xarm-python-sdk xarm/x3/linear_motor.py:221-240).

After a hold or an error the example sends nothing more, so stop() does not run and the track stays enabled until a person checks it. The guide asks for cleanup on errors too (docs/contributor_guide/device-driver-guide.md:23); what is safe to send after an unknown outcome is an open point.
sources: xArm Python SDK API doc, master branch (linear motor calls)
